Key findings The Oct 14 result reads back consistently: 64,700 t is 23,963 BCM x 2.7, and the 89,700 t month-to-date gap is 33,222 BCM x 2.7. 7. The "89,000 meters behind" in the Notion summary of the client review is tons of production, not drilling. 8. Drilling record conflict: month-to-date shows 10,315 m ahead (HOD) while a drill stood 4 h and excavators stood for lack of muck. 9. Drilling stock closed Oct 14 at 18,476 BCM. Lost volume: one excavator stood 5 h on Oct 14 for no loading area, about 1,580 BCM / 4,266 t at the 316 BCM/h fleet average (Oct 13 rate, estimate). Drill hours have no meters-per-hour rate in the sources, so not converted. Client scenario: year-end 19.25 Mt with no change, 19.91 Mt with Fridays plus two excavators, 20 Mt only with hot seating (12 operators, from Nov 1), 6 rental 777 trucks plus a PC1200, and a single North Dump. Client version due Sunday Oct 18, review Monday Oct 19. The DT-Requirement deck family (v8) recommends 4 to 5 extra trucks; the Oct 15 scenario asks for 6 rental trucks. No tonnage is given for the combined scenario. Flagged in the article. Safety and security: hard hat rule restored for everyone outside at dispatch, magazine blast radius to camp unconfirmed (2.5 km estimated), evacuation plan issued (345 people to evacuate). Task Feedback Log queried newest first. Latest row is dated 2026-10-10 and every row is Processed. No resolutions, no mismatches, nothing to mark. Notes & References scanned (50 rows). New: Q4 Dump Truck Requirements & Action Plan Review 2026-10-15 and Night Shift Handover Summary 2026-10-14. Updated: Project Meeting Stage 4/5 Priority 2026-10-14 (edited after its RAW copy; `-revised` file written). All other rows already in RAW with no later edits. Which unit the 435,000 / 410,000 targets carry. Which scenario is the client figure of record (deck v8 vs the Oct 15 combined scenario). "Armor 102" unidentified. Drilling meters record versus parked drills. Stage 6 access still needs blasting first.
